dct_description_sm: Detailed studies to date of the bioaccumulative effects of total mercury (THg) on northern fishes have focussed on all but one of the key species consumed by humans. The exception is the Dolly Varden (Salvelinus malma) char (DVCH) prized as a food resource in the western Canadian Arctic. THg can accumulate in the environment and in large, top predators such as DVCH, and can represent a significant threat to human health. Because of the predicted rates of environmental change occurring in the Arctic as a result of climate change and industrial development, it is necessary to document THg baselines in DVCH to better understand the significance of any future changes in THg levels.
